summary: People who own guns disagree among themselves, one calling it a right that must not change and another a privilege that can be licensed.
realLife: In interviews with gun owners after a school shooting, one said the right to bear arms should never change and that armed teachers would deter attackers. Another said school shootings are rare and the attacks are unstoppable. A third called ownership a privilege and would accept age limits, checks and a driver-style test, while doubting they would work at scale. A fourth wanted vetting for AR-15-style rifles and national standards. Three of the five doubted new laws would stop attacks.
sources: https://www.michiganpublic.org/2022-05-28/what-some-gun-owners-are-saying-in-the-wake-of-americas-latest-mass-shooting (NPR piece of five gun owners, via a member station)
